title: Infrastructure Engineering Playbook: GPU Fleet, Networking, IaC, CI/CD, and Runbooks
author: Jordan Alvarez
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference infrastructure engineering standards and operational runbooks for GPU fleet & capacity, cloud accounts & networking, Terraform/IaC modules, CI/CD build pipelines, and common infra runbooks. It is intended as the canonical starting point for on-call engineers, infra owners, and new hires.

Scope: Covers production and pre-production environments for hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Does not replace team-level design documents (link to design reviews in related pages).

Ownership and Contacts

- Infra Platform (primary owners): infra-platform@redwood-inference.com
- GPU Fleet Team: gpu-fleet@redwood-inference.com (primary on-call rotation listed in PagerDuty)
- Networking & Cloud Accounts: cloud-networking@redwood-inference.com
- CI/CD & Build: infra-ci@redwood-inference.com

High-level Principles

1) Single source of truth: Terraform modules + module registry for all cloud resources.
2) Immutable artifacts: container images and AMIs are built once and promoted across environments.
3) Predictable capacity: reserve base capacity for production SLOs, use autoscaling for bursts.
4) Observability-first: dashboards and alerts must exist for every critical service and autoscaler.

GPU Fleet & Capacity

SLO & Capacity Targets

- Production 99th percentile p99 token latency target: 150 ms (per model-class SLA).
- Baseline reserved capacity: sized to handle 80% of expected peak QPS per region.
- Burst capacity: additional autoscale pool that can add up to 2x baseline within 10 minutes.

Node types & sizing

- gpu-a100-40gb: primary for high throughput models; used in Dedicated clusters.
- gpu-a10g-24gb: primary for inference and mixed workloads.
- gpu-t4: cost-efficient for small models and background jobs.

Autoscaling policy (recommended)

1) Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) on per-service basis using queued requests and GPU utilization metrics.
2) Cluster autoscaler for node pool scale-outs with target grace period 600s.
3) Minimum lane nodes: keep min nodes equal to baseline reserved capacity; scale down windows 30m to avoid noisy churn.

Capacity planning process (quarterly)

1) Forecast demand using three signals: usage growth (weekly active requests), model onboarding schedule (product calendar), and historical per-token cost.
2) Run capacity simulation using perf-suite (see /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite) with representative prompt mixes.
3) Propose commit changes to finance for Dedicated reserved contracts 45 days before quarter start.

GPU Fleet Operations Runbooks (summary)

- Capacity exhaustion (high queue length)
  1. PagerDuty alert fires: "gpu-cluster-queue-length-high".
  2. Verify metric: cluster-level queued request count > 300 for 5m and GPU utilization > 85%.
  3. Actions: scale node pool (terraform or cloud console), trigger manual spillover to lower-cost regions, or enable model fallback policy from Console.
  4. Post-incident: update capacity model and adjust autoscaler thresholds.

- Node OOM / GPU failure
  1. Identify failing node via node exporter and cloud provider errors.
  2. Evict pods on node: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
  3. Replace node via autoscaler or recreate machine image if hardware appears faulty.
  4. Add to incident ticket and notify hardware provider if repeated.

Cloud Accounts & Networking

Account structure

- Organization structure: root org -> billing accounts per region -> environment accounts (prod, staging, dev) -> service-specific projects (e.g., redwood-gpu-prod-1).
- Central shared services account hosts: CI/CD runners, Bastion, logging, cost export, and monitoring.

VPC and network topology

- One VPC per environment per region with standardized subnet layout (public app-subnet / private service-subnet / GPU-subnet).
- GPU-subnet enforces route tables that restrict direct internet egress; NAT gateway in shared services account handles outbound.
- Peering/Transit: use cloud provider Transit Gateway or VPC Peering for cross-account communication. All peering requests must be reviewed and approved by network owners.

Security & Connectivity

- RBAC: minimal IAM roles for service accounts; use short-lived credentials where possible.
- Private endpoints for control-plane services (e.g., artifact registry, secrets manager).
- KMS-backed disk encryption for GPU instances; HSM/KMS per customer for Private deployments as required.

Network runbook snippets

- Verify VPC reachability: iperf3 and traceroute from bastion.
- Recreate NAT gateway: terraform apply -target=module.nat_gateway

Terraform / IaC Modules

Module standards

- Registry: internal module registry at registry.redwood-inference.internal (modules must include README, examples, inputs/outputs).
- Versioning: semantic versions (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH). Modules must have CHANGELOG.md and PR template requiring a backward-compatibility check.
- Naming: modules/resource names should use short prefixes: rwi- (redwood infra) e.g., rwi-gpu-nodepool, rwi-vpc, rwi-k8s-cluster.

Example usage (Terraform HCL snippet):

resource "rwi_gke_node_pool" "gpu_pool" {
  name          = "gpu-pool-a10g"
  machine_type  = "a10g-24gb"
  gpu_count     = 1
  min_nodes     = 5
  max_nodes     = 50
  autoprovision = true
}

Module CI rules

- All modules must have: terraform fmt, terraform validate, unit-test plan, and integration plan against a sandbox account.
- PR gates: automated diff review, cost-estimate, and security-scan (check for hard-coded secrets).

CI/CD & Build Pipelines

Pipeline design patterns

- Build once, promote many: images are built in the CI account and promoted to registries for staging/prod.
- Canary deployments: supported by infra pipelines using feature flags and 10% traffic rollout by default.
- Blue/green for critical infra components (e.g., control plane) with automated smoke tests.

Key pipelines

- Image build pipeline: builds base images (packer/kaniko), signs artifacts, publishes SBOM.
- IaC pipeline: runs plan in sandbox, then runs gated plan/apply in target accounts using ephemeral runners.
- Cluster deploy pipeline: accepts image tag and module version; runs canary then promotion.

Typical CI commands

- Build image: ./ci/build-image.sh --tag=sha-<short-hash>
- Run terraform plan: ./ci/terraform-plan.sh --env=staging --module=rwi-gpu-nodepool

Runbooks (detailed examples)

1) GPU capacity exhaustion (detailed)
- Trigger: alert "gpu-pool-remaining-capacity" and queued requests > 250
- Action steps:
  a) Confirm via Prometheus dashboards (gpu-cluster/queue-length, node-pool/available-nodes).
  b) Temporarily scale node pool: terraform apply -var='extra_nodes=20' -target=module.rwi-gpu-nodepool
  c) If terraform not available, use cloud console to add instance group members.
  d) Fallback: change routing policy in Redwood Console to route lower-priority customers to best-effort pool.

2) Build pipeline failure (image promotion)
- Trigger: pipeline fail on signing or SBOM mismatch.
- Action steps:
  a) Check CI logs and artifact registry.
  b) Re-run build with --debug and collect logs.
  c) If signing key expired, contact security@redwood-inference.com to rotate key.

Team Wiki & Documentation Hygiene

- Templates: use the infra doc template for runbooks, design docs, and incident reports.
- Ownership: every page must list owner_team and at least one primary author.
- Reviews: quarterly doc reviews requested by doc owners; set review reminders in Confluence.

Appendix: Useful Commands and Dashboards

- kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
- gcloud compute instances create --machine-type a2-highgpu-1g --accelerator type=nvidia-a100,count=1 ...
- terraform plan -var-file=environments/prod.tfvars
- Prometheus dashboards: infra/gpu-capacity, infra/network-latency, ci/pipeline-health

Postmortem & Change Process

- Any production incident impacting SLOs must have a postmortem within 7 days with RCA, impact, and action items. Link postmortems to this playbook.
- Infrastructure changes that alter capacity or network topology must follow the RFC process and have a scheduled maintenance window (win: 02:00-05:00 UTC for region).
